title: Overnight: impact measured as you see it, and a compiler that delivers more of it
summary: Your three rounds of blind pair judgments settled what impact means: how much a hit changes the rider's whole-body motion (its direction, speed and spin) within 50 ms. The old measure agreed with you no better than chance (31/63); the new one agreed on 46/63. A floor-then-rail bounce now counts as two impacts, as you see it.

Overnight, the compiler was tuned against that measure, one hypothesis at a time, judged on every measure on two panels and confirmed on fresh arrangement seeds. Compared with this evening's product, on all four panels: impact loss −60%, strong beats much closer to their request, double impacts almost gone, fewer head-down arrivals into strong hits, and speed accuracy unchanged. The cost: air accuracy about 0.005 worse and about 15% more physics per ride.

The rest of the gap is mostly physics or the spec itself. The rider does not survive a clean hit much above 0.9, the gentlest touchdown reads about 0.06, and the densest song asks for back-to-back maximum hits faster than gravity can supply the momentum. Those are questions for you, below.

cards.title: The measure (line.strike.v3)
cards.text: Strength = whole-body motion change, travel and spin, in 50 ms. Floor-then-rail opposite pushes are separate impacts. Chosen on your blind pairs; proven equal to the judged measure.

cards.title: Steep, upright arrivals
cards.text: Before a strong beat the rider now arrives steep and fast, but not head-down: strong-beat shortfall −0.03 on top of the new objective, speed error −0.02, head-down strong arrivals 30% → 15%.

cards.title: Search where it matters
cards.text: The lookahead widens ×1.3 into strong beats (+0.3M frames). A native read of the rider's motion makes every compile 20% faster, byte-identical.

cards.title: Tried and set aside
cards.text: Pose-matched catches, sharper turns, guided dives, speed headroom, more weight on impact or air or quiet beats, more learned proposals: each measured, each a trade or null (see the ledger).

questions: Scale: should a request of 1.0 mean the hardest hit the rider survives (about 0.9 today), and 0 the gentlest touchdown (about 0.06)? Today both ends of the 0–1 scale are out of physical reach, so the extremes always miss.

L’amour de ma vie asks for back-to-back hits of 0.9 or more about 13 frames apart, its intro asks for speed the start cannot give, and its tail asks for low air with a strong hit on every beat. Re-author, or treat these as stretch goals?
Air against impact: weighting air 1.5× recovers this evening's air accuracy but gives back about a third of tonight's strong-beat gain. Which matters more to you?
Lines passing visibly through the rider (6–8 per ride, July none) and the rider's body dragging along rails: worth fixing? A short look at the examples would tell.
When you have five minutes: a blind pair session comparing this evening's and tonight's hits on random strong beats (link below).
